The results showed no overall first night effect on severity of RMMA frequency in young and healthy patients with SB. This suggests that there is currently no conclusive evidence to support or refute the presence of a first night effect on sleep bruxism.

However, for patients with moderate-high frequency SB (RMMA), one-night sleep recording may still be sufficient for monitoring their condition, as the results indicate that low RMMA frequency in the first night could potentially be confirmed by a second night based on individual patient factors.
